about.title: Personal Injury Help in Mountain View, California
about.longDescription: Mountain View is bracketed by US-101 and SR-85, with El Camino Real and Shoreline Boulevard carrying much of the everyday traffic in between. That geometry shows up in the public record. In 2025, the most recent year with final figures, the city logged 422 injury collisions. Those crashes left 565 people hurt and 2 people dead. The corridors with the highest collision counts were US-101, El Camino Real, SR-85 and Shoreline Boulevard, and reported crashes tended to peak on Thursdays between 6 p.m. and 8 p.m. Statistics describe traffic, though, not the person who now has a neck brace, a totaled car and an adjuster calling before breakfast. If that is you, it helps to know how this works. We handle personal injury claims in Mountain View and Santa Clara County. We can review what happened, whether it was near the Computer History Museum on Shoreline or on a quiet residential street. We take cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. Reaching out costs nothing, and you decide what happens next.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Mountain View Claim

items.title: The clock is usually two years
items.desc: California gives most injury claims a two-year statute of limitations, but the window can be as short as six months when a city, county or state agency is involved. Sorting out which deadline applies early avoids an unpleasant surprise later.

items.title: Partial fault does not close the door
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, being partly to blame reduces what you can recover rather than wiping it out entirely. We can help make sure your share of fault is assessed fairly.

items.title: Pain and suffering is not capped
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain, lost sleep and the things you can no longer do. Those losses count, and they can be part of a claim.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: We work on contingency, so you do not pay hourly rates or up-front retainers. Our fee comes out of a recovery, and only if there is one.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in California?
items.answer: Most personal injury claims in California must be filed within two years of the injury. If a government entity is involved, such as a city vehicle or a public roadway defect, the deadline can be as short as six months. Because the rules differ, it is worth confirming your specific deadline as soon as you can.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the crash?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault. That means your recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault, but you are not barred from recovering just because you share some blame. Even a driver found mostly responsible may still have a claim for the remainder.
